problem:
Find ${e}^{At}$ for $A=[\begin{aligned}-3 & -10 \\ 5 & 7\end{aligned}].$ 

*Hint: The eigenvalues of $A$ are $2\pm 5\text{i}.$*

| ${e}^{At}={e}^{2t}\,\,$ |  | {{field-1}} | $-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t)$ |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | {{field-2}} | $\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t)+\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t)$ |  |  |
worked_solution:
We have a square matrix of dimension $n=2.$ Thus, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{At} & ={\alpha }_{1}At+{\alpha }_{0}I \\  & ={\alpha }_{1}[\begin{aligned}-3 & -10 \\ 5 & 7\end{aligned}]t+{\alpha }_{0}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3{\alpha }_{1}t+{\alpha }_{0} & -10{\alpha }_{1}t \\ 5{\alpha }_{1}t & 7{\alpha }_{1}t+{\alpha }_{0}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

where ${\alpha }_{1}$ and ${\alpha }_{0}$ are functions to be determined.

Consider the polynomial $r(\lambda )={\alpha }_{1}\lambda +{\alpha }_{0}.$ The eigenvalues or $At$ are 

$$
{\lambda }_{1}=(2+5\text{i})t,\,{\lambda }_{2}=(2-5\text{i})t,
$$

which are complex conjugates. Thus, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}r((2+5\text{i})t) & ={e}^{(2+5\text{i})t} \\ {\alpha }_{1}(2+5\text{i})t+{\alpha }_{0} & ={e}^{2t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t)+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t)) \\ (2{\alpha }_{1}t+{\alpha }_{0})+5{\alpha }_{1}\text{i}t & ={e}^{2t}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t)+\text{i}\,{e}^{2t}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we equate the real and imaginary parts, and solve for ${\alpha }_{1}$ and ${\alpha }_{0}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}2{\alpha }_{1}t+{\alpha }_{0}={e}^{2t}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t) \\ 5t{\alpha }_{1}={e}^{2t}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t)\end{aligned}\,⇒\,{\begin{aligned}{\alpha }_{1}=\frac{1}{5t}{e}^{2t}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t) \\ {\alpha }_{0}={e}^{2t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t)-\frac{2}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t))\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${\alpha }_{1}$ and ${\alpha }_{0}$ into the expressions for the required entries of ${e}^{At},$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}-3{\alpha }_{1}t+{\alpha }_{0} & =-3\cdot \frac{1}{5t}{e}^{2t}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t)\cdot t+{e}^{2t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t)-\frac{2}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t)) \\  & =-\frac{3}{5}{e}^{2t}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t)+{e}^{2t}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t)-\frac{2}{5}{e}^{2t}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t) \\  & ={e}^{2t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t)-\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t)) \\ 5{\alpha }_{1}t & =5\cdot \frac{1}{5t}{e}^{2t}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t)\cdot t \\  & ={e}^{2t}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
{e}^{At}={e}^{2t}[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t)-\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t) & -2\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t) \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(5t) & \operatorname{sin}⁡(5t)+\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t)\end{aligned}].
$$
